notes.meaning: Saul stayed in Damascus for a long stretch of time, which included a trip to Arabia and back, lasting about three years. His bold and steady preaching made his opponents so angry that they plotted to take his life. The man who had once hunted down believers was now being hunted himself.

Saul discovered the plot against him before his enemies could strike. Because Damascus was surrounded by a high protective wall, his opponents guarded every gate day and night to catch him trying to leave. God preserved Saul's life by allowing the secret scheme to come to light.

Some local believers came to Saul's aid under cover of darkness. They placed him in a large basket and lowered him down the outside of the city wall through an opening or window. Escaping in this way allowed Saul to preserve his life while remaining faithful to the Lord's calling.

When Saul returned to Jerusalem three years after his conversion, he tried to join the believers there. The Christians were terrified of him and could not believe he had genuinely changed. They remembered his cruel persecutions and worried he was pretending in order to trap and arrest them.

Barnabas stepped forward with great kindness and courage, bringing Saul directly to the apostles Peter and James. He explained how the Lord Jesus had personally appeared to Saul on the road, and how fearlessly Saul had preached in Damascus. Thanks to Barnabas speaking up for him, the leaders welcomed Saul as a true brother.

The believers in Jerusalem welcomed Saul into their fellowship, and he stayed with them for about two weeks. He moved freely throughout the city, praying and worshipping alongside the other disciples. He spoke openly about Jesus, no longer held back by the fear of others.

Saul shared the good news about Jesus with Greek-speaking Jews, the very group that had earlier clashed with Stephen. Saul answered their objections and argued that Jesus is truly the Messiah, God's promised Savior. Instead of listening, his opponents became enraged and planned to murder Saul just as they had murdered Stephen.

Once the believers learned about this assassination plot, they acted quickly to protect Saul. They escorted him down to the seacoast at Caesarea and put him on a ship to his hometown of Tarsus. Saul would continue serving God and preaching the gospel among his own people there.

With Saul's conversion and departure, open persecution died down, giving churches across the whole region a season of calm. The believers grew stronger as they lived with deep reverence for God and enjoyed the comfort and encouragement of the Holy Spirit. As a result of this healthy spiritual life, the church continued to multiply.

Taking advantage of this peaceful time, Peter traveled from town to town to encourage the scattered believers. He came down to the town of Lydda, about a day's journey west of Jerusalem. The believers living there are called saints, a word meaning people set apart and dedicated to God.

In Lydda, Peter met a man named Aeneas who had been paralyzed and unable to leave his mat for eight full years. His long illness was well known in the community and completely incurable by human medicine. His desperate condition showed how great God's power was when healing came.

Peter did not claim any power of his own, but announced that Jesus Christ was healing Aeneas right at that moment. He told the man to stand up and roll up the sleeping mat he had lain on for years. Aeneas rose immediately, giving visible proof that he was entirely restored.

differ.view: Miracles of physical healing through individuals were special signs given to confirm the apostles' message during the foundation of the church.
God continues to perform miraculous healings through believers today as the Holy Spirit directs.

notes.meaning: Aeneas's sudden healing was so obvious and real that crowds of people in Lydda and across the plain of Sharon saw him walking. This extraordinary sign demonstrated to everyone that the gospel message was true. Seeing the power of Christ firsthand, a great number of people turned from their old ways and believed in the Lord.

In the coastal seaport of Joppa, there was a faithful believer named Tabitha, whose Greek name was Dorcas, meaning gazelle. She spent her days actively caring for people by doing kind deeds and giving help to the poor. She lived out her faith through generous action rather than mere words.

other.label: Orthodox
other.view: Tabitha is honored as a widow who spent her remaining years in faithful ministry and charity within the Joppa church.

notes.meaning: Despite her usefulness and holy life, Tabitha became sick and died. Her friends washed her body in the usual way to prepare for burial, but then carried her to an upstairs room. Keeping her there instead of carrying her out to a tomb right away showed they held a glimmer of hope that God might intervene.

Lydda was only a short journey of a few miles from Joppa. When the believers heard Peter was there, they immediately sent two men to plead with him to come without any delay. Having heard of Aeneas's healing, they wanted Peter's presence and ministry in their deep sorrow.

Peter went with the messengers as soon as they asked him. When he arrived in the upper room, a group of weeping widows gathered around him, pointing to the shirts and coats Dorcas had sewn for them while she was alive. Their tears and handmade garments showed how deeply she was loved and how greatly she would be missed.

Peter sent everyone out of the room so he could seek God in quiet prayer, just as Jesus had done when raising Jairus's daughter. Peter knelt down to pray, showing that the power belonged to Christ alone and not to him. After praying, he told her to get up, and she opened her eyes and sat up.

differ.view: Miracles such as raising the dead were unique signs of an apostle given to confirm the gospel message in the early church, and are not a normal gift today.
The supernatural power of the Holy Spirit to heal the sick and raise the dead was not limited to the apostles, and God still performs such miracles through believers today.

notes.meaning: Peter took Tabitha by the hand and helped her to her feet. Then he called back the believers and the weeping widows, presenting her to them alive and completely well. Their deep mourning instantly turned into great joy and gratitude to God.

The news of Tabitha being restored to life spread quickly throughout the entire seaport of Joppa. The miracle served its true purpose by confirming the good news about Jesus that the apostles preached. Convinced by what God had done, many people put their faith in the Lord.

Peter stayed in Joppa for quite some time, choosing to lodge in the home of a man named Simon, who worked as a leather tanner. Tanners handled dead animal hides, a job that strict Jewish customs looked down upon as ceremonially unclean. By staying with Simon, Peter showed humble love and took an important step past old social barriers, preparing him for the wider work ahead.
